title: a-measurement-answers-a-question-under-its-own-name
author: cc
intention: A measurement can answer an open question through the question door, recorded as answered by that measurement and citing the record it read, never as Akien.
what: A measurement can answer an open question through the question door, recorded as answered by that measurement and citing the record it read, never as Akien.
why: Law 9 (ruling 2026-08-15): 'anything settled by measurment trumps approvals by even me'. The question door's only answer writes 'Akien' into answered_by, so a question measurement already settled either waits at his gate — the binding constraint (2026-09-15) — or carries his name on words he never said. Measured 2026-09-23: 9 open questions settled by measurement with no honest way to close them.
traces_to: Law 9; CP1 (a record that says Akien answered when he did not is a confabulation).
how: One keyword on question.answer, one flag on its CLI; everything else rides the existing answer path. THE BUILD SPEC IS THE decisions LIST: D1..D4.

falsifier.proves_red: RED while the only answered_by the door can write begins 'Akien', or while a measured answer can cite a record that does not exist.
falsifier.proves_green: GREEN: one tooth — (a) a measured answer resolves, names its record, keeps the class suffix last, journals 'a measurement answered'; (b) a nonexistent record is refused and nothing resolves; (c) the CLI --measured path answers and show carries it.
falsifier.horizon: one proof run at PROVEME; reverting the keyword reds the tooth.

watchme: none, because the falsifier is discharged whole by the proof at PROVEME (cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question.py) and every use afterwards is already watched: each measured answer is a journaled record whose answered_by names its record, and the existing probe cairn/tools/question/probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py reads answered_by on every crossing — the same disposition as PROVED ticket 5ef45e513849.

decisions.text: D1 THE KEYWORD. cairn/tools/question/question.py answer() gains `measured: str | None = None` (keyword-only, after spawned_why). When given, it must be a non-empty string naming an existing file — checked with Path(measured).expanduser().is_file() from the caller's cwd, stored exactly as given; otherwise it joins the SAME `lacks` list the other refusals use, so one Refused names every lack and nothing is written. On success: answered_by = f"measurement: {measured}, recorded by caller class {who['class']}" (the class suffix stays LAST — the probe at probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py:63 reads the last token); the record also gains `"measured": measured`. Without measured, answered_by is byte-identical to today's 'Akien, recorded by caller class <c>'. `spawned` stays required either way; `words` are the finding in the recorder's words.

D2 THE JOURNAL WHY. The _write(...) why reads 'a measurement answered <id>' for a measured answer and 'Akien answered <id>' otherwise, followed by the unchanged spawned suffix — the journal and the record must not contradict (Law 5). Same verb, `answer`.

D3 THE CLI. cairn/tools/question/__main__.py: the `answer` subparser gains `--measured <record>` (optional), passed straight to Q.answer(measured=...); the module docstring gains the line `cairn question answer <qid> "<the finding>" --measured <record> --spawned none`. No new verb.

D4 THE TOOTH. One tooth in cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question.py, keyed under THIS ticket id in PROVES as clause 'all' (one composite tooth) and named test_a_measurement_answers_under_its_own_name, run in teeth_door over the same scratch world: (a) open a question, write a scratch record file inside tmp, answer with measured=<that path> → resolved, answered_by startswith 'measurement: <path>' and endswith 'caller class <c>', record['measured']==path, and the last journal 'answer' entry's why contains 'a measurement answered'; (b) open another, answer with measured=<tmp>/does_not_exist.json → Q.Refused, and the question reads back unresolved; (c) the CLI over _env(qdir): open, then `answer <id> <words> --measured <path> --spawned none` exits 0 and `show` contains 'measurement: '. The module docstring gains a line for it. The charter cairn/tools/question/intention+why.json gains the measured path in its invoke line, through `cairn artifact write --verb cast`.

D1's placement stands as measured: answer()'s signature today is answer(qid, words, *, spawned=None, spawned_why=None, root=None) (cairn/tools/question/question.py:184) — spawned_why exists, and measured goes between it and root.

D4's two pieces, spelled: teeth_door(tmp) is a FUNCTION in cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question.py, not a framework — the new tooth is a sibling function teeth_measured(tmp) called right after it inside main()'s same TemporaryDirectory, using that file's own helpers (Q, A, check, _env, PROVES); and the charter edit is MANUAL — the builder writes the amended intention+why.json to scratch by hand (invoke line gains measured=None and the --measured CLI form; entry gains one dated sentence) and passes it through `cairn artifact write cairn/tools/question/intention+why.json --verb cast --why ... --from <file>`, which journals the write and syncs nothing from code.

The tooth's shape, exactly as the file's existing teeth are written: PROVES is a dict {ticket_id: {clause: tooth_name}} — add "c62df2454322": {"all": "test_a_measurement_answers_under_its_own_name"}; check(name, ok, detail) prints PASS/FAIL and appends to FAILURES; a tooth is a plain function that builds its inputs and ends in ONE check(PROVES["c62df2454322"]["all"], ok_a and ok_b and ok_c, detail). Q is cairn.tools.question.question, A is cairn.tools.artifact.artifact (A.read_journal(commons) returns the journal entries as dicts with 'verb' and 'why'); _env(qdir) returns the subprocess environment for the CLI at REPO/bin/cairn. main() calls teeth_measured(Path(d)) inside its own try/except that on any exception calls check(...all, False, repr(exc)), so a reverted subject reds this tooth only and not its siblings.

The charter's two fields are plain JSON strings: "invoke" is one long string listing Python calls then CLI forms — replace the substring 'Q.answer(qid, words, spawned=[...]);' with 'Q.answer(qid, words, spawned=[...], measured=None);' and append after the answer CLI form the text '`cairn question answer <qid> "<the finding>" --measured <record> --spawned none` (answered_by reads `measurement: <record>`, never Akien; Law 9, ticket c62df2454322),'; "entry" is a prose string — append one sentence beginning 'Extended 2026-09-24 under ticket c62df2454322:'. No other field changes.

The 'who' in D1's answered_by is the local already in answer() today: `who = door.caller()` (question.py, a few lines above the record.update), where door is cairn.tools.artifact.artifact and caller() returns a dict whose 'class' is the kernel-measured cgroup class ('cc', 'akien', 'gate'). D1 adds no parameter for it; it reuses that local unchanged.

_write is a module-level function in question.py, not a method (there is no Question class): _write(path, record, *, verb, why) — answer() already ends in `_write(_path(record['id'], root), record, verb='answer', why=f"Akien answered {record['id']}" + <spawned suffix>)`. D2 changes only the leading f-string: f"{'a measurement' if measured else 'Akien'} answered {record['id']}". _write's signature is untouched.

The --why for D8's charter write is exactly: "c62df2454322 D4: invoke and entry name the measured answer path" — the door journals it verbatim; any why naming the ticket id is accepted, and this is the one used.
